description: 40 frozen Landing Zone anti-patterns, paired one-to-one with capabilities.

criteria.title: Shadow tenants and unmanaged orgs
criteria.description: Production lives in extra directories, organizations or personal accounts that the platform team cannot inventory or govern.
sub_criteria: Do production workloads exist in tenants, organizations or accounts outside the declared root?
Is there no maintained inventory of extra directories or billing relationships?
Are mergers, partners or 'temporary' clouds still running production without a landing-zone owner?

criteria.title: Workloads in the management plane
criteria.description: Applications, data lakes or developer sandboxes sit in the management, payer or tenant-root subscription. A landing-zone change now risks the company.
sub_criteria: Are application resources deployed in the management, payer or bootstrap account?
Would a landing-zone rebuild require migrating production out of that plane first?
Do app teams have standing contributor rights on the management plane?

criteria.title: Billing split from technical ownership
criteria.description: Finance pays a bill that platform cannot map. Technical owners cannot name the contract. Scope debates replace assessment.
sub_criteria: Can platform and finance not agree which subscriptions, accounts or projects are in-scope?
Are invoices received for clouds that have no landing-zone owner?
Is cost allocation blocked because billing structure does not match the hierarchy?

criteria.title: Unbounded guest or partner access at root
criteria.description: External identities hold owner-equivalent rights at tenant, organization or management-account level with no expiry.
sub_criteria: Do guest, partner or vendor identities hold owner-equivalent roles at the root?
Is that access standing (no expiry, no dual control)?
Is there no review of external admin at the organization plane?

criteria.title: Unowned root credentials
criteria.description: Root, super-admin or Global Admin credentials are shared, unlogged, or known only to a departed person.
sub_criteria: Are root or super-admin credentials shared, stored in email, or unused-and-unknown?
Is there no MFA or hardware key on the cloud root?
Would the estate be unrecoverable if one person left?

criteria.title: Standing root-equivalent access
criteria.description: Humans hold permanent Global Admin, AdministratorAccess or organizationAdmin. Privilege is a lifestyle, not an event.
sub_criteria: Do humans hold standing owner-equivalent roles at tenant, org or account root?
Is there no activation, time-bound or approval step?
Is that population larger than a named break-glass set?

criteria.title: Local cloud users as primary identity
criteria.description: People log in with cloud-native users disconnected from the corporate IdP. Leavers keep access. Joiners get a second identity to babysit.
sub_criteria: Are cloud-local human users the normal way to access the estate?
Does leaver processing in the corporate IdP leave cloud access intact?
Are shared logins (team@, admin@) in use?

criteria.title: Long-lived keys as identity
criteria.description: Access keys, client secrets and downloaded service-account keys are how automation and people authenticate. Rotation is a wish.
sub_criteria: Are long-lived access keys or JSON service-account keys the default for workloads or humans?
Are keys older than policy (or unaged) still valid?
Do pipelines store cloud credentials in variables rather than federate?

criteria.title: Unscoped Owner at root
criteria.description: Application teams receive Owner, Editor or AdministratorAccess at the organization or management-group root 'so they can work'. Guardrails cannot hold.
sub_criteria: Do application teams hold owner-equivalent rights at the organization or management-group root?
Can they disable policy, networking or logging as a side effect of that grant?
Is there no alternative scoped role for daily delivery?

criteria.title: Unmonitored or missing break-glass
criteria.description: Either emergency access does not exist, or it exists and nobody would notice if it were used — or abused.
sub_criteria: Is there no designed emergency-access path?
Is emergency access used as a daily convenience account?
Would use of emergency access produce no alert?

criteria.title: Flat subscription or account sprawl
criteria.description: Hundreds of subscriptions, accounts or projects hang off the root. Policy cannot inherit. Nobody can draw the map.
sub_criteria: Do most isolation units sit directly under the tenant, org root or a single catch-all node?
Is the hierarchy unused as a policy spine?
Can the platform not produce a current map of nodes and owners?

criteria.title: Applications in the platform landing zone
criteria.description: Business systems share the connectivity, identity or management subscription. Platform change freezes the business; business change risks the platform.
sub_criteria: Do application workloads share platform subscriptions, accounts or projects?
Would a platform rebuild collide with application data?
Are application teams granted rights on platform landing zones to 'get things done'?

criteria.title: Ad-hoc naming and tag theatre
criteria.description: Names are local jokes. Tags exist in a PDF. Create-time enforcement is absent. Search, cost and incident response guess.
sub_criteria: Do names and tags differ by team with no enforced standard?
Is the tagging standard documentation-only?
Are untagged resources treated as acceptable?

criteria.title: ClickOps birth of isolation units
criteria.description: Subscriptions, accounts or projects are created in the portal, emailed into existence, or copied from a neighbour. Baseline is optional.
sub_criteria: Is the normal create path a portal click or a ticket to a human who clicks?
Do new units appear without policy, logging or network baseline?
Is there no record of who requested the unit and why?

criteria.title: Mixed environments in one boundary
criteria.description: Production, test and playground share a subscription, account or folder. A playground identity can reach production data.
sub_criteria: Do production and non-production share the same isolation unit?
Can non-production identities reach production data or keys?
Is 'we use resource groups / VPCs instead' used to avoid a landing-zone line?

criteria.title: Per-application internet edge
criteria.description: Every team brings its own public IP, firewall flavour and VPN. The platform cannot see, inspect or retire paths.
sub_criteria: Do application teams create their own public IPs, firewalls or VPNs as the normal path?
Is egress inspection optional per team?
Is there no inventory of internet edges?

criteria.title: Flat global network
criteria.description: Everything can route to everything. Segmentation is a slide. A compromised sandbox reaches production.
sub_criteria: Can every spoke route to every other spoke by default?
Is production reachable from non-production on the network?
Are NSG/SG/firewall rules effectively allow-any?

criteria.title: Split-brain or absent private DNS
criteria.description: Each team runs DNS. Private endpoints do not resolve. Hybrid names work 'on my laptop'. Incident response cannot find things.
sub_criteria: Is private DNS missing, or different in every landing zone?
Do private endpoints fail to resolve without tribal knowledge?
Are hosts files and tribal resolvers in production use?

criteria.title: Public as the default
criteria.description: Storage, Kubernetes API, databases and jump hosts are public unless someone remembers to tick a box. Policy does not deny it.
sub_criteria: Are public endpoints allowed by default on data, control-plane or jump services?
Is there no deny policy for public access?
Is the public inventory unknown?

criteria.title: Unmanaged peering mesh
criteria.description: Peerings, attachments and interconnects accumulate. Nobody can draw the current topology. A delete is an outage lottery.
sub_criteria: Is the current network topology not drawable from inventory?
Do peerings and attachments exist without an owner or change record?
Would removing a 'temporary' path have unknown blast radius?

criteria.title: Optional security
criteria.description: The baseline is a PDF. Teams may enable Defender, GuardDuty or SCC 'when they are ready'. Most are not ready.
sub_criteria: Is the security baseline advisory rather than assigned?
Can a landing zone be vended with threat detection off?
Is 'we'll add security later' visible in the last N vended units?

criteria.title: Per-subscription SIEM islands
criteria.description: Each team has a log workspace, a GuardDuty detector, or a SCC project. Nobody can hunt across the estate. Retention is a guess.
sub_criteria: Are detections and security logs fragmented per landing zone with no org view?
Is there no delegated security administrator at organization scope?
Would a SOC hunt require asking every team for access?

criteria.title: Keys in code or unused CMK theatre
criteria.description: CMK is claimed in architecture decks while disks use default keys and API keys sit in Git. Encryption is a brand.
sub_criteria: Are customer-managed keys claimed but not actually in use on data stores?
Do repositories or pipelines contain live cloud keys?
Is there no key-access logging or rotation?

criteria.title: Secrets in pipelines and wikis
criteria.description: The secret store is Azure DevOps library, GitHub Actions secrets used as long-lived cloud keys, Confluence, or a shared spreadsheet.
sub_criteria: Are production secrets stored in CI variable groups, wikis or chat?
Are those values long-lived cloud credentials rather than federated identity?
Is rotation manual and overdue?

criteria.title: Security as an after-the-fact ticket
criteria.description: Workloads go live, then a security questionnaire is filed. Findings have no landing-zone owner. Platform and SOC point at each other.
sub_criteria: Does security review start after the workload is in production?
Are cloud findings unowned between platform and SOC?
Is there no security landing zone to host org controls?

criteria.title: Logs left in the subscription
criteria.description: Activity logs stay in the producing account, expire at default, and disappear. Forensics starts with 'we no longer have that'.
sub_criteria: Are organization activity logs not exported from the producing landing zone?
Is default retention the de-facto policy?
Would an incident older than a few weeks be unreconstructable?

criteria.title: No current inventory
criteria.description: The estate map is a draw.io from a previous consultant. New accounts appear in the invoice first.
sub_criteria: Is there no API-fresh inventory of isolation units?
Do invoices or workshops discover accounts the platform did not know?
Is policy assignment state unknown?

criteria.title: Application monitoring only
criteria.description: APM is excellent. The logging pipeline, ExpressRoute, org trail and policy engine have no owner and no alert.
sub_criteria: Are platform-plane services unmonitored while applications are?
Would a failed log export be noticed only in an audit?
Is there no platform on-call?

criteria.title: No platform restore
criteria.description: Application backup is mature. The landing zone IaC state, DNS and keys have one copy on one laptop.
sub_criteria: Is platform configuration unrestorable except by tribal knowledge?
Is Terraform/Bicep/Pulumi state on a laptop or an unversioned storage account?
Have restores never been rehearsed?

criteria.title: Snowflake agents and images
criteria.description: Every team brings an agent, an image, and an exception. The platform cannot patch, observe or retire them.
sub_criteria: Are guest agents and images unmanaged exceptions as the default?
Can the platform not tell what is running on compute it hosts?
Is drift from the golden image invisible?

criteria.title: Policy as documentation only
criteria.description: There is a beautiful standard. Nothing in the control plane assigns it. Workshops recite it. The API does not.
sub_criteria: Is the guardrail set documented but not assigned in the control plane?
Do new landing zones boot without the baseline?
Is 'we plan to enable policy next quarter' the current state?

criteria.title: Root-level allow-all
criteria.description: The only org-level policy is FullAWSAccess, an empty initiative, or restoreDefault. Prevention lives in goodwill.
sub_criteria: Is the effective organization policy equivalent to allow-all?
Can any landing zone disable logging, attach public IPs, or leave the org?
Are denies present only in a lab?

criteria.title: Permanent exemptions
criteria.description: Whole management groups, OUs or folders are excluded 'for now'. Now is three years old. The excluded node holds production.
sub_criteria: Are hierarchy nodes excluded from policy with no expiry?
Does the excluded node contain production?
Is the exemption undocumented or owned by a departed person?

criteria.title: No cost or region guardrail
criteria.description: Any region, no tags, no budgets. The landing zone will happily host a GPU farm in an unapproved geography.
sub_criteria: Can resources be created in any region without policy friction?
Are tags optional?
Do landing zones have no budget owner?

criteria.title: Screenshot compliance
criteria.description: Evidence of control is a PDF of a dashboard, a workshop assertion, or a vendor questionnaire. The control plane was not queried.
sub_criteria: Is compliance evidenced only by slides, questionnaires or screenshots?
Was the control plane not queried for this assessment?
Do findings say 'we believe we are compliant' without an export?

criteria.title: ClickOps platform
criteria.description: The landing zone exists in the portal. Code, if any, is an export from last year. The next change will be another click.
sub_criteria: Is the platform primarily configured in the console?
Is IaC absent, stale, or generated after the fact?
Would a rebuild from code fail?

criteria.title: Email-request vending
criteria.description: A landing zone is an email to a named person who has Owner at root. Cycle time is weeks. Quality is mood.
sub_criteria: Is the create path an email, chat or ticket that ends in a human clicking the portal?
Is cycle time unmeasured or measured in weeks?
Do vended units differ depending on who was on shift?

criteria.title: Drift accepted
criteria.description: Code and cloud parted ways. Apply would be destructive, so nobody applies. The repository is literature.
sub_criteria: Would an IaC apply be unsafe because reality has moved?
Is there no drift detection, or is drift ignored?
Is the repository no longer the system of record?

criteria.title: Ticket-only, no self-service
criteria.description: Every spoke, DNS record and exception is a platform-engineer hour. The landing zone does not scale because the platform team is the bottleneck.
sub_criteria: Must every landing-zone request go through a platform engineer performing the work?
Is there a catalog item that nobody uses?
Is onboarding time dominated by platform wait?

criteria.title: Undocumented hotfixes
criteria.description: Production was saved at 2 a.m. in the portal. The code was not updated. The next apply will undo the save — or nobody will ever apply again.
sub_criteria: Are production platform hotfixes done in the portal without a follow-up change in code?
Is there no break-glass record?
Would the next pipeline run surprise production?
